Remember this, my friend, as someone who is 34 and had to go back to college so late that I graduated last year, but with two degrees. If I could do it all over again at your age, I would want to know these things:

1. Everything is a skill, skills require time to get better at. Not everything you'll be good at, but you can become good at everything, with time.

2. "Hard choices now, easy life later.:" - Jimmy Carr

3. Do extracuricuriculars like they're side quests in video games. Not necessary for the journey, but if you want the best experience end game, you need to do them.

4. Read. Everyday. Even if it's just one chapter of a book. Read. For the love of god. Harry Truman couldn't do school, and was completely self taught. He just read everything he could. He became president of the United States. The world  is your oyster.

5. Friends are temporary, but family is, too. Treat every experience you have with them as if they were your last. You never know when you'll be forced to say goodbye.

Keep your head up. Build your routines. You'll make it and do great things.

I do not know you, but I love you, as a human being, as the start of adulthood for your generation, I wish you nothing but the best of luck.

You can make your own luck, though. Again, with time.

P.S: Watch Goodwill Hunting until you don't want anything to do with that life. Please. It will help you keep going.
